# Native personhood documentary references

This additive profile connects the original Artist operation-24
personhood head to an exact original General identity notarization. It provides
checkable documentary linkage for AA-IDENTITY 8, CMC-ATTESTATIONS 11 and
CMC-MUSEUM-GRADE 2(f). It does not establish legal personhood, institutional
standing, instrument validity, or factual truth. Signer verification and those
external trust questions remain distinct.

The implementation has source and test-oracle review plus a 2,630-source
Solidity 0.8.19 ABI/type/storage check. Original production ABI entries and
recursive storage layouts are preserved. The 28 behavioral cases are authored;
execution, contract size, transaction gas and complete current-stack acceptance
remain pending. This is not complete Museum acquisition evidence.

## Original selection authority

The original `recordArtistAttestation` operation is the only fresh selector.
Use subject kind 10, the actual primary Artist ID, its operative identity record
hash, and the unchanged `6529STREAM_ARTIST_PERSONHOOD_EVIDENCE_V1` schema.
Original op24 signatures, nonce guards, authority classes, native record hashes,
events, owner commit and Archive transaction boundaries remain unchanged.
`StreamArtistC2PACredentials.note`, already called inside op24 and complete op60
imports, retains the derived proof in the same transaction. There is no new
external owner mutation, independent selector, signature, or nonce.

The statement is the separately pinned, closed 590-byte JSON interpretation
generated by `StreamArtistPersonhoodJSON`. Its eight ordered keys bind original
Artist Registry, Artist ID, operative identity record, General host/runtime and
record hash, profile hash, and version. Existing native statements and hashes
are not rewritten. An old opaque evidence statement stays historical and has
status UNRESOLVED; a later C2PA credentials record does not replace, satisfy,
or erase this schema-specific personhood head. Explicit waiver behavior remains
the original election.

Register the exact new interpretation document as CATALOG name
`STREAM_ARTIST_PERSONHOOD_REFERENCE_JSON_PROFILE_V1`, using original Schema
Registry governance, RAW_BYTES canonicalization, and supersedes zero. Its source
is `schemas/records/STREAM_ARTIST_PERSONHOOD_REFERENCE_JSON_PROFILE_V1.json`:
1,837 bytes including LF, Keccak-256
`0x06eaf449a0abe6a4305706d589bc597f14f7d23f62acc661b4b1fff128b921c3`.
Do not replace any previously registered schema/profile under its original ID.
The original notarization schema, JSON profile, and RFC8785 definitions are
independently checked against their original literal hashes and full bytes.

## Full proof at recording

A canonical new reference requires the actual Core-selected Module Registry,
an ACTIVE General module of original type/version/interface/runtime, reciprocal
Core and Artist Registry pins, and the issuer's exact selected notarization
head. The proof reads the complete original General record/receipt, original
subject tuple, payload, signature bundle, receipt inventory position and schema
definitions. It independently rebuilds the original record and authorization
preimages. It requires the original institutional/estate signer-verified
notarization family and exact original identity Registry/Artist/operative
identity facts; a generic self-assertion or native Artist-labelled statement
cannot substitute.

Collection, token and media subjects use the original `StreamIndependentReads`
constants and field order. No invented subject domain is introduced. The
original producer verified the signature when the immutable receipt was
recorded. This proof preserves that recorded result; it does not call today's
ERC1271 owners to reauthorize an old signature or infer an issuer's external
institutional standing.

After full verification, a 48-word immutable `Summary` binds the native record,
statement, Artist, original Registry/code, binding/generation/collection,
operative identity, reference, Core/Module/Schema/Store pins, immutable document
facts, exact report head key, documentary hash, module identity and six retained
carrier/code hashes. The six carriers are report payload, signature bundle and
the four exact single-chunk definitions. The native record's summary hash is
`keccak256(abi.encode(keccak256("6529STREAM_ARTIST_PERSONHOOD_PROOF_SUMMARY_V1"), summary))`.
An additive event and original payload-store carrier retain this documentary
preimage for reconstruction. Neither is a new authority record.

## Bounded currentness versus documentary audit

Read the actual fixed Attribution owner selected by the normal Artist
Registry/Coordinator suite. This capability adds no Registry facade selector.

| Method | Contract |
| --- | --- |
| `personhoodEvidence(collectionId,artistId)` | Original native head, retained reference/provenance, live status and head facts. |
| `personhoodEvidenceStatus(collectionId,artistId)` | Compact original native hash and the same status for the prospective floor. |
| `personhoodProofSummary(nativeRecordHash)` | Immutable validated summary; zero version means none. |
| `personhoodProofSummaryHash(nativeRecordHash)` | Independently retained hash, checked against stored summary bytes. |
| `auditPersonhoodEvidence(nativeRecordHash)` | Full documentary replay and original hash comparison, separately from mint currentness. |

Currentness rechecks the actual owner/suite, current accepted binding and
generation/hash, current operative identity, original Registry/Core/General/
Module/Schema/Store runtime pins, all six immutable carriers, actual current
Module Registry pointer, General catalogue identity/lifecycle, original document
facts, and the same recorder-scoped General head. It never follows a newer head.
It never copies a mutable payload into a trusted cache. Full documentary data
was validated once at original op24 and remains behind immutable producer,
schema and carrier identities. The full audit deliberately rereads those bytes.

The compact serving path uses the existing raisable ARTIST_SALE_FACTS_READ_GAS
row, including its original failure class and full EIP-150 forwarding precheck.
Full admission/audit/import uses the existing ARTIST_FINALITY_READ_GAS row.
No cap, floor, gas default or caller-controlled allowance is raised here. Cold
execution within the original Manager/Artist budgets is unmeasured and remains
a required post-approval test; avoiding repeated documentary replay is an
architecture choice, not a numerical gas claim.

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| NONE | No native personhood head. |
| WAIVER | Original explicit waiver remains current for actual identity/generation. |
| RESOLVED | The exact admitted documentary summary remains current under all bounded joins. |
| STALE | A prior admitted record has a known identity/binding/head/lifecycle/definition/code mismatch. |
| UNRESOLVED | Opaque legacy data, missing proof, or malformed/unavailable bounded reads. |

DEPRECATED permits inspection of immutable prior documentary evidence; it does
not admit a fresh reference. INCIDENT_REVOKED and unknown modules cannot supply
RESOLVED status. Known mismatches retain the original selected evidence as STALE;
failed reads are explicit UNRESOLVED. There is no hidden fallback to another
notary, recorder, native head or later credential record.

The prospective Museum floor is intentionally stricter: evidence-schema heads
must return their exact native hash with RESOLVED status, or the existing
explicit waiver must apply. Historical opaque evidence does not establish the
checkable identity notarization required by CMC-ATTESTATIONS 11 / CMC-MUSEUM-GRADE
2(f). Original record getters, retained bytes and historical acceptance facts
are unchanged; this proposal does not retrospectively claim that old floor
checks verified documentary linkage.

## Original domains across migration

Complete authenticated operation60 imports retain original native and General
Registry domains. The original journals, record hashes, nonce/replay history,
owner headers, complete supplied rows and one-shot all-seven-owner transaction
remain the import authority. For each canonical evidence row, the fixed importer
locates the actual original Registry's Coordinator and Attribution owner through
reciprocal immutable suite facts and copies that owner's exact summary and
retained hash. It independently joins native record, statement, Artist,
collection, binding, generation, operative identity, original reference and
Core/runtime pins before storing anything authoritative. The existing op60 guard
must already be installed; there is no alternate summary writer.

Missing capability, absent summary, malformed encoding, changed hash, foreign
Registry/Artist/collection or substituted identity is a whole-import refusal,
not a false empty head. Opaque legacy and waiver rows stay their existing
historical profiles without inventing proof. Supported old typed row encodings
and original hashes do not change; the new derived namespace is mandatory for
canonical evidence and is atomically retained with its original owner data,
payload tail and Archive. Any late source or Archive failure rolls all of it back.

An imported original General record can remain inspectable in its original
domain after Artist cutover. A fresh successor op24 must name the successor's
own Registry domain and a genuine notarization admitted for that identity
configuration; it cannot promote the imported old reference into fresh authority.

## Authored validation and pending evidence

The test fixture uses actual Artist owners/facade/Archive, threshold
Safe, General Attestations, Schema Registry and Store. Core/Metadata/governed
action context and explicit negative read/code injections remain typed fixture
boundaries. Tests author original record/event preimages, exact summary/hash,
full-versus-bounded read separation, original subject domains, stale/new issuer
heads, legacy/waiver/credentials isolation, missing definition, signature-history
preservation, runtime/schema/carrier/identity drift, original op24 replay,
missing/forged import summaries, complete migration, late Archive rollback and
identical Safe retry. The first type check caught a fixture cheatcode-interface
mismatch; the test now uses the existing typed `avm.mockCall` interface. The
subsequent 2,630-source check passes. Behavioral execution, capacity and
current-graph acceptance remain pending.

### Rollback and retention oracles

The 28 authored cases include distinct op24 and op60 late-Archive failures.
The op60 case uses the actual Archive uint64 block bound and requires exactly two
append calls across the failed attempt and identical successful retry. The retry
alone cannot satisfy this counted expectation. The append is after all seven
owner imports. A separate missing-row early-refusal control requires exactly one
append across its refused attempt and completed-input retry, proving that this
early failure is not counted as a late Archive attempt.
It compares all seven checkpoints (including nonce/replay roots and counts),
hydration commitments, native receipt counts, history activation commitment,
personhood selection and summary, Identity/Attribution/Consent/Archive payload
counts, source state and Safe nonce. After restoring the block, it submits the
exact same target calldata through the actual Safe and requires the seven
matching nonzero completion commitments. Reverted inspector observations are
not treated as durable logs; only successful retry logs are folded.

Fresh recording and completed import independently reconstruct the tagged
summary ABI bytes and require one `ARTIST_PERSONHOOD_PROOF_SUMMARY` catalog row
in both the actual Attribution owner and Archive. The two catalogs must name
the same immutable carrier with exact STOP-prefixed length and code hash.
The successful `ArtistPersonhoodProofRetained` event must have the actual owner
emitter, original native record and Registry topics, schema version, summary
hash and every complete Summary field. These assertions fail if the new summary
retention or event is removed while the older documentary carriers remain.

`testFuzzCanonicalJsonRoundTrip` is a same-codec roundtrip fuzz recipe, not an
independent differential implementation. The fixed profile bytes, native and
summary preimages, catalog/event checks and malformed-input controls are separate
oracles. These cases remain unexecuted; gas, capacity, current-stack and full
acquisition-conformance acceptance are not established.

The late-failure test counts both Archive attempts. A successful retry alone
cannot satisfy the assertion; the separate early-refusal control expects only
one attempt. Both tests still require execution against the fitting joined graph.

docs/guides/artist-recovered-authority-h.text:
# Recovered Artist authority hydration

## Implementation status

The developing operation-60 profile 10 adds the explicit
`hydrateRecoveredArtistAuthority(StreamArtistRecoveredHydrationTypes.Request)`
entry point. Its seven-owner masks remain `0x7f`. Existing hydration selectors
keep their existing profiles and exclusions.

This is a source implementation with ABI-only checks. The seven concrete owners
advertise feature mask 63 for these graphs; the base owner stays disabled. The positive
import scenarios are authored but have not run. Safe execution, current-stack
integration, bytecode size, gas, invariants and release acceptance remain pending.

The first graph is one recovered class-1 or class-3 Artist, one accepted
generation-one PRIMARY_ONLY collection, no collaborators, base Attribution,
and complete direct operation-14 policy history. An explicit economics extension
also carries complete direct operation-15 history for that same binding.
Complete Identity and Payout histories are transported together. Class 4,
multiple Artists or collections,
collaborator graphs, corrected generations and broader collection histories
remain separate full-v1 obligations. A capability bit does not bypass these
typed source restrictions.

| Feature bit | Required source state |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | Current or retained recovery class 1 |
| 2 | Current or retained recovery class 3 |
| 4 | Retained V2 preparation evidence |
| 8 | Retained V3 evidence or recovery continuations |
| 16 | More than one retained import era |
| 32 | Complete direct economics history, selected by actual native operation 15 |

Every source and destination owner must support the combined required mask.
Pending requests, compromised status and unused preparations are included in
the typed graph; feature bits do not silently discard them.
These transport feature bits grant no Artist permissions. An original estate
authority capability mask, including a zero mask, remains unchanged.

## Request and source admission

`Request.records.authority` supplies the complete Artist and collection
selectors, expected source checkpoints and logical replay-key preimages. Without
economics history, `records.witnesses` must remain empty. A source with
operation-15 records requires exactly one witness for the selected collection,
containing all economics terms in original operation-15 order and no attestations.
Missing, extra, duplicate or reordered terms reject. Empty wrappers also reject.
The request also names every expected source capability, the exact prior import
commitment, and a nonzero expected semantic inventory.

The fixed Coordinator authenticates the current governed predecessor and its
seven-owner suite. The source must be sealed by its actual operation 57 naming
this destination. The destination must have its genuine operation 55 binding
and operation 56 verified lanes before hydration. A lane proof alone does not
install authority. The non-Artist dependencies must still match.

`StreamArtistRecoveredHydrationPrepared.prepare` constructs the read-only
certificate and performs the same source checks used by the mutation path.
`inventory` hashes its complete provenance, query, seven owner payloads, timing
checkpoint and external guard observations. The caller supplies this identifier
as `expectedSemanticInventory`. The mutation route uses `collect`, which
rejects a zero or changed identifier. This helper is a fixed Solidity library;
the Registry does not expose a separate preparation endpoint.

## Retained records and clocks

Historical record bodies, signatures, hashes and stored local revisions remain
unchanged. Each retained native occurrence carries its original environment,
owner index, admitted owner revision and original native index. Repeated
secondary operation 35 receipts retain distinct occurrences even when their
record hashes are equal. Preparations and execution operations 32/40 have
original mutation points, not synthetic native receipts.

Each destination stores a flat immutable prefix plus its own actual native
suffix. An A→B→C transport carries A's original coordinates and B's original
coordinates directly. Runtime readers compare authenticated era order before
comparing revisions within the same owner and era; they never compare A's raw
revision to B's raw revision. A copied record with a large old revision cannot
be treated as a new destination record merely because that number exceeds the
destination import revision.

An owner imports only its own typed state, provenance slice, nonce inventory
and publication catalog. The Coordinator performs the full seven-owner join,
including Payout's original Identity35 and nonce dependencies. Fixed typed
adapters authenticate auxiliary creation points from actual producer state.
Missing imported origin metadata is an error.

## Replay, nonces and retained dependencies

All indexed nonce kinds, keys, prefixes and words are carried. Current replay
cells are authenticated against the actual source checkpoint and their logical
surface/scope preimages. Rekeyed live cells retain their original mutation
point until an actual destination write updates them. Historical source 55 and
source 56 cells remain recorded. Genuine destination 56 latches retain their
local cells; source 57 stays historical so the destination can later seal its
own cutover.

Original document and signature carriers retain their SSTORE2 pointers and
bytes. The complete source catalogs are admitted before semantic imports;
the normal Coordinator payload synchronization registers them with the new
Archive. Full timing configuration and timing-action history are inventoried
separately from the original owner checkpoint.

Governance actions, finality recovery records and entropy observations remain
on their original pinned hosts. Their exact observations are bound into the
certificate and checked again after destination writes. Hydration does not
reset an external consumed guard or turn an old preparation into a current
execution authorization. New authorizations use the destination's existing
signer and governance domains; retained history is read under its original
producer domain.

## Direct economics composition

The economics extension requires capability bit 32 on every source and destination
owner. The complete original Consent-owner journal must contain only direct
operations 14 and 15. Economics terms are limited to the original fixed primary
or royalty resolver, generation 1 and the exact accepted Artist/binding pair.
Delegated and corrected-generation economics remain separate profiles.

The fixed source authenticates each economics record through its original payload
lookup, exact binding association, native occurrence and consumed replay cell.
All three economics maps survive import. The retained row does not contain the
signer, nonce, observed time or historical payout hash, so the importer does not
invent those fields or reconstruct the record from current facts. The complete
Identity export separately retains the original signature and nonce admissions;
the complete Payout export retains its own history. Their revisions are separate
owner clocks and are never equated.

Every old economics replay cell remains consumed in every later import era, with
its original admission point. Historical approvals remain recorded when current
payouts or assignments change. Import does not rerun mutable assignment checks.
Fresh operation 15 still checks the current principal, signature domain, payout
and assignment; class-3 authority still needs its original economics permission.

## Atomicity and transport bounds

Each original owner import commits exactly once at its actual revision + 1.
Hydration adds no original native record. The source provenance, publications,
timing and external guards are rechecked after all seven writes. The
Coordinator then appends paged evidence and the canonical operation 60 header,
followed by the existing history and payload synchronization. Any propagated
failure rolls back the entire transaction.

Transport is finite: at most 16 source eras, 4,096 total native occurrences,
8,192 replay aliases, 128 indexed nonce lanes per owner and 256 prefixes per
lane. Evidence uses at most 128 pages of 20,480 bytes. These bounds reject an
oversized new import; they do not cap future original writes or runtime reads
after a successful import. A destination may operate with the maximum imported
prefix plus its own additional current era.
The economics extension admits at most 128 complete operation-15 records and
128 direct policy selectors for the selected collection.

## Validation boundary

Authored cases cover provenance and replay guards, full nonce payloads,
publication preservation, separate timing, external observations and precise
auxiliary origins. The actual class-1 fixture uses the original seven owners,
Registry, Coordinator, Archive and Safe. It covers A→B→C, unchanged original
operation-35 evidence, fresh guardian writes, C operations 29/30/32, governed
C operation 33, current V2 preparation and recovery, stale source rejection,
and exact late Archive rollback/retry. Four additional class-3 cases retain
original activation40 and recovery35, preserve a zero estate capability mask and an
unused scheduled action, and author fresh successor rotation and recovery.
Two V3 cases transport the original mixed rewind plan across all six
non-guardian families and its guardian exclusion. They check complete retained
records, statuses, operative heads and continuations, stale Payout rejection
with identical retry, and fresh operations 25/18 consuming the original
continuations under genuine destination clocks. The source retirement remains
contested, so fresh operation 51 must retain its exact original rejection;
these cases do not establish a positive operation-51 flow.
Additional V3 scenarios transport class-3 authority with a fresh signed operation
25, and import A→B→C after B consumes A's revision and payout continuations. C keeps
those cells spent and authors ordinary current-chain writes after the original
recovery window matures.
Three economics cases author genuine mature recovery, signed payout and mixed
primary/policy/royalty consents before import. They cover A→B→C with a fresh
prospective economics consent in B, retained approvals under C's current domain,
exact replay rejection with nonce rollback, malformed witnesses, and a late
Archive failure followed by an identical Safe retry. Thirteen component cases
cover the economics codec, maps, complete journal, aliases, counters and old/new
feature dispatch; their typed coordinator and synthetic second-era cases do not
establish full-host authorization. A separate capability case rejects economics
imports on any owner advertising only the first-graph features.
Core and governance fixtures remain explicitly typed unit boundaries.

ABI-only compilation establishes source and type compatibility. It does not
establish that these transactions execute, fit deployment limits or meet the
protocol's gas and security acceptance criteria.
